name: BURKINA FASO

flag.title: Flag of Burkina
flag.note: Red & green halves, gold star at centre

lead: Burkina Faso is a landlocked country in West Africa with six neighbours and no coast. Its name means "Land of Upright People." A president chose it because he thought honesty mattered most. Most people are farmers. Sunsets over the flat land glow gold.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Burkina Faso is a high, flat land about 400 m above sea level. Three rivers cross it: the Black Volta, Red Volta, and White Volta. Rain turns dust into green savanna almost overnight.
The highest peak, Mount Tenakourou, is only 747 m. From the top, you can see Mali and Ivory Coast. The dry Sahel region creeps south each decade, so planting trees is vital.
animals: The W-Arly-Pendjari area has about 200 elephants, 100 lions, hippos, and 300+ bird species. Elephants wade the Arli river at dawn.
At Bazoulé, 30 km from the capital, over a hundred Nile crocodiles share a sacred pond with villagers.
culture: Over 60 ethnic groups live here, and all make music and masks. The Mossi, Bobo, and Bwa peoples carve tall wooden masks of ancestors and animals.
Every two years, Ouagadougou hosts FESPACO, Africa's biggest film festival. Directors from 50+ countries compete for a prize, the Golden Stallion of Yennenga, named after a Mossi princess.
history: The Mossi kingdoms ruled from around 1100 CE. France ruled the land as a colony called Upper Volta from 1896. It became independent on 5 August 1960.
Captain Thomas Sankara took power in 1983. In 1984, he renamed the country and planted 10 million trees. Soldiers seized power and killed him in 1987.
wows: Burkina Faso's name blends two local languages: 'upright' in Mooré, 'fatherland' in Dyula.
FESPACO in Ouagadougou has been Africa's largest film festival since 1969.
Villagers treat the 100+ Nile crocodiles at Bazoulé as sacred.
From Mount Tenakourou's summit you can see three countries.
Burkina Faso is a top-15 gold producer, yet most people farm.
Sankara's team vaccinated 2.5 million children in one week, without foreign aid.
Burkina Faso has six neighbours, among the most in West Africa, but no sea.

myths.fact: Shea butter comes from the nuts of the shea tree. Many women in Burkina Faso make it by hand.

myths.myth: Burkina Faso is hot all year
myths.fact: From December to February, the cool, dusty Harmattan wind blows in from the Sahara.
